name: Light Lavender
lede: Light Lavender is a very pale violet, a lightened lavender, and as a painted color it is almost absent from the museum record.

sections.title: Lavender, lightened
sections.body:
Lavender is itself a pale color. Paterson's dictionary defines it as violet mixed with white, and uses it, with pink, as an example of a color of low saturation [1]. Light Lavender goes one step further in the same direction [1]. Our library draws it from the xkcd color survey and from the ISCC-NBS system of 1955, block 222 [2].

Its nearest learnable neighbor is [[lavender]], about nine units away, and it sits near [[lilac]] and [[violet]] [2]. Compare [[light-grey-green]] for another lightened name [2]. The name is descriptive, so the coiner is undocumented [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Painting almost never uses it. At a looser test, a color within four units covering even one per cent of a canvas, no painting among 23,781 in our archive qualifies [3]. Pale violets are mostly tints inside skies, skin and drapery rather than flat areas [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the result describes our archive, not painting as a whole [3].

questions.q: According to Paterson, lavender is a mixture of which two colors?
True or false: our archive holds many paintings in which Light Lavender covers 1 per cent of the canvas.

openers: Lavender is violet plus white, and Light Lavender adds still more white.
